scope: Frontend, four-language catalogs, landing guides and demo-only sample coordinates on the existing 1.4.1 Debian installation. API image remains 1.4.2.
changes: Demo opens directly without visitor-location guidance, browser permission or country admission. Existing website consent remains shared.

All 50 browser-local sample accounts and admin/operator builders provide supported locations. All 125 demo/E2E Mongo profiles, including group profiles, have finite points inside their supported country geometry.
Demo sessions retain sample coordinates: automatic visitor tracking and cached visitor-login location are excluded. Explicit location editing remains available.
Sign-in with missing location opens the existing permissions popup directly; the optional guide remains available through its existing launcher.
External browser navigation uses the existing Android handoff, preserves campaign URLs, and now uses the dark ink menu palette and emphasized explanatory text.
Short EN/HU/DE/ES notices omit the misleading Chrome appearance comparison. Landing guides distinguish own-account location from demo sample coordinates; notifications and installation are optional.

frontendTestBatches.note: Entry tests rerun after the direct-popup change; 125 distinct latest cases across the seven suites.

verification.productionBuild: Angular production build passed. The full frontend tree is identical before/after squash; only normal build metadata and service-worker precache stamping were refreshed for the final commit.
verification.seedGeometry: All 125 demo_db and 125 e2e_db profiles checked against their actual country polygons; browser-local builders tested against the existing country resolver.
verification.migration022: Actual deployed mongosh compiled the final migration against a no-write DB stub; demo-only migration and idempotence/retention oracle passed.
verification.manualDeviceInteraction: No user-owned browser navigation, external-browser tap or native permission interaction was replayed.

migrationAttemptAudit: The first unpublished migration022 attempt was a no-op on production and failed before demo writes because mongosh compiled an optional method call incorrectly. The validation was corrected and checked in actual mongosh. Its production no-op record retains the original SHA256 and correction reason; the demo step then completed. Earlier released migration files and inputs were retained.
retentionNotes: No production users were added or removed. One pre-existing user devices field changed during runtime observation; other production profile fields were unchanged. Runtime telemetry and notification histories continued. Fourteen demo location projections were restored while all demo activity/lifecycle fields and all 947 media objects remained unchanged.
